title: NCERT School Book Quiz
description: Original English-language NCERT-aligned concept practice for Classes 6–12. These questions are not copied from NCERT textbook exercises or represented as official NCERT answer keys.

source.publisher: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
source.linkPolicy: Consult the official NCERT catalogue to choose the current class, subject, medium and edition. No unit/page-level source alignment has been claimed. NCERT textbooks are copyrighted and are not hosted or reproduced here.

sets.subject: Science
sets.topic: Scientific thinking, materials and living things

questions.question: Which tool is most suitable for measuring the length of a notebook?
questions.explanation: A ruler directly measures a small object's length in centimetres or millimetres.

questions.question: What is the usual SI unit for mass?
questions.explanation: The kilogram is the SI base unit of mass; a litre measures volume.

questions.question: Which of these is transparent?
questions.explanation: Transparent materials allow light to pass through so objects behind them can be seen clearly.

questions.question: Which process separates insoluble sand from water using filter paper?
questions.explanation: Filtration traps insoluble particles while the liquid passes through the filter.

questions.question: Which characteristic is common to living organisms?
questions.explanation: Response to stimuli is a characteristic of life; organisms differ widely in form and colour.

questions.question: Which body part allows most fish to take dissolved oxygen from water?
questions.explanation: Gills exchange gases with surrounding water in most fish.

questions.question: What generally happens to ice when heated above its melting point?
questions.explanation: Heating ice beyond its melting point changes its state from solid to liquid.

questions.question: Which material is usually attracted to a bar magnet?
questions.explanation: Iron is ferromagnetic and is attracted to an ordinary magnet.

questions.question: What does a closed electrical circuit allow?
options: A bulb to glow without energy
questions.explanation: A closed conducting loop allows current to pass through components.

questions.question: Which is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is continually replenished by the Sun, unlike fossil fuels.

questions.question: What is the place value of 7 in 47,205?
questions.explanation: The digit 7 occupies the thousands place in 47,205.

questions.question: What is the greatest common factor of 18 and 24?
questions.explanation: The common factors of 18 and 24 include 1, 2, 3 and 6, so the greatest is 6.

questions.question: Which fraction is equivalent to one half?
questions.explanation: Multiplying numerator and denominator of 1/2 by 3 produces 3/6.

questions.question: What is 2/3 + 1/6?
questions.explanation: Use a common denominator of 6: 2/3 becomes 4/6, then 4/6 + 1/6 = 5/6.

questions.question: What is 15% of 200?
questions.explanation: Fifteen percent means 15 per 100, so 0.15 × 200 gives exactly 30.

questions.question: How many degrees are in a right angle?
questions.explanation: A right angle measures exactly 90 degrees.

questions.question: What is the perimeter of a rectangle 8 cm long and 5 cm wide?
questions.explanation: Perimeter adds all four sides: 8 + 5 + 8 + 5 = 2 × (8 + 5) = 26 cm.

questions.question: What is the area of a square of side 7 cm?
questions.explanation: Area of a square is side × side = 7 × 7 = 49 square centimetres.

questions.question: What is the smallest prime number?
questions.explanation: Two is prime because it has exactly two positive factors: 1 and 2.

questions.question: A number divisible by both 2 and 5 must end in which digit?
questions.explanation: A number divisible by 5 ends in 0 or 5; divisibility by 2 also requires an even last digit.

questions.question: Which line divides Earth into Northern and Southern Hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Equator is the reference latitude at 0 degrees and divides Earth into north and south.

questions.question: What does a map scale show?
options: Relationship between map distance and ground distance
Number of people in a city
questions.explanation: Scale expresses how a distance on paper corresponds to a real-world distance.

questions.question: Which direction lies opposite east?
questions.explanation: East and west are opposite cardinal directions.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a globe?
options: Show a single street in high detail
questions.explanation: A globe models Earth's broadly spherical shape and the relative positions of large features.

questions.question: Which water body contains most of Earth's surface water?
questions.explanation: Oceans contain by far the largest share of Earth's surface water.

questions.question: Why were many early settlements located near rivers?
options: Access to water and fertile land
questions.explanation: Rivers supplied water, food resources, transport opportunities and fertile floodplains.

questions.question: What is the main use of archaeological evidence?
options: Learn about past human activity from material remains
questions.explanation: Artefacts, structures and remains help reconstruct how people lived in the past.

questions.question: What is a manuscript?
questions.explanation: Manuscripts are handwritten records, often preserved on paper, palm leaves or other materials.

questions.question: Which is an example of a primary historical source?
options: A fictional film set in the period
An inscription from the period studied
questions.explanation: An inscription produced in the period provides direct historical evidence.

questions.question: What is meant by a community?
options: People connected by shared location or social relationships
Only people born on one day
questions.explanation: Communities involve groups of people linked by place, relationships or shared interests.

questions.question: How is heat transferred through a metal spoon placed in hot tea?
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers thermal energy through the solid material of the spoon.

questions.question: Which type of substance turns blue litmus red?
questions.explanation: Acidic solutions turn blue litmus red under normal indicator conditions.

questions.question: What is the usual colour of red litmus in a basic solution?
questions.explanation: Basic solutions turn red litmus paper blue.

questions.question: Which gas do green plants usually absorb during photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Plants take in carbon dioxide and use light energy to synthesise carbohydrates.

questions.question: What do stomata mainly help regulate?
questions.explanation: Stomata permit gas exchange and control much of the water loss through leaves.

questions.question: Which device is used to measure temperature?
questions.explanation: A thermometer measures temperature rather than pressure, current or length.

questions.question: What is the main role of roots in most terrestrial plants?
options: Absorb water and minerals and anchor the plant
questions.explanation: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and mineral ions from soil.

questions.question: What happens to a shadow when the light source is blocked by an opaque object?
options: A dark region forms behind the object
Light passes entirely through the object
questions.explanation: Opaque objects obstruct light and form shadows on surfaces behind them.

questions.question: What process transfers pollen from anther to stigma?
questions.explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains to the receptive stigma.

questions.question: Which is the correct unit of speed?
questions.explanation: Speed is distance travelled divided by time taken.

questions.question: What is (−6) + 9?
questions.explanation: Starting at −6 and adding 9 gives positive 3.

questions.question: What is 3/4 of 48?
questions.explanation: One quarter of 48 is 12; taking three such quarters gives 3 × 12 = 36.

questions.question: What is 0.25 expressed as a percentage?
questions.explanation: Multiply a decimal by 100 to convert it to a percentage.

questions.question: If x + 7 = 19, what is x?
questions.explanation: Subtract 7 from both sides of the equation to get x = 12.

questions.question: Which number is the additive inverse of −13?
questions.explanation: The additive inverse sums with the original number to give zero.

questions.question: What is the supplementary angle of 65°?
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles add up to 180 degrees: 180 − 65 = 115.

questions.question: A shirt priced ₹500 is discounted by 10%. What is the selling price?
questions.explanation: Ten percent of ₹500 is ₹50; the new price is ₹450.

questions.question: What is the mean of 4, 7 and 10?
questions.explanation: The sum is 21 and there are 3 numbers, so the arithmetic mean is 7.

questions.question: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.explanation: Triangle area is one half × base × perpendicular height.

questions.question: Which property states a + b = b + a?
questions.explanation: Commutativity means changing the order of addends does not change their sum.

questions.question: What is a historical chronicle?
options: A record of events arranged over time
questions.explanation: Chronicles narrate events and can provide evidence about the periods and authors who produced them.

questions.question: Which of these is a renewable natural resource when managed sustainably?
questions.explanation: Forests can regenerate under sustainable management; fossil fuels form over geological timescales.

questions.question: What is erosion?
options: Removal and transport of weathered material
questions.explanation: Erosion moves soil or rock through agents such as water, wind or ice.

questions.question: What is the principal purpose of a constitution?
options: Replace all local laws each day
Set basic rules and institutions of government
questions.explanation: A constitution establishes the framework for governance and key principles of public authority.

questions.question: What is a local government body in an Indian village called?
questions.explanation: Gram Panchayats are local self-government institutions at the village level.

questions.question: Which factor most directly influences rainfall through the water cycle?
questions.explanation: Water vapour condenses into cloud droplets that may later fall as precipitation.

questions.question: Which statement best describes equality before law?
options: Only officials are subject to law
Similar legal standards apply irrespective of social status
Courts must treat every case identically regardless of facts
questions.explanation: Equality before law rejects arbitrary privilege and requires lawful treatment.

questions.question: What does a primary economic sector involve?
questions.explanation: Farming, fishing and mining are examples of primary-sector activities.

questions.question: What is a market in economics?
options: Arrangement where buyers and sellers exchange goods or services
A place that only sells vegetables
A building that cannot host trade
questions.explanation: Markets can be physical or digital settings in which exchange occurs.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate method to check a historical claim?
options: Compare the claim with reliable contemporary evidence
Judge by the number of emojis
questions.explanation: Source criticism weighs provenance, context and corroborating evidence.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of force?
questions.explanation: A newton is the SI unit of force, named after Isaac Newton.

questions.question: Pressure is defined as what quantity?
questions.explanation: Pressure equals normal force divided by the area over which it acts.

questions.question: Why do sharp knives cut more easily than blunt ones?
options: They exert greater pressure over a smaller area
questions.explanation: A smaller contact area concentrates the applied force, increasing pressure.

questions.question: Can sound travel through a vacuum?
options: No, because sound requires a material medium
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave transmitted by vibrations of matter.

questions.question: What part of the human body vibrates to produce voice?
questions.explanation: Air passing through the larynx causes the vocal folds to vibrate.

questions.question: Which process creates a new substance?
questions.explanation: Rusting is a chemical reaction in which iron forms iron oxides.

questions.question: Why are ball bearings used in machines?
options: To reduce sliding friction by rolling motion
questions.explanation: Rolling contact often produces less friction than sliding contact.

questions.question: Which phenomenon is responsible for hearing an echo?
questions.explanation: An echo occurs when reflected sound reaches the listener after a noticeable delay.

questions.question: Why is a lubricant added between moving machine parts?
questions.explanation: Lubricants form a film that lowers friction between surfaces.

questions.question: What is the usual SI unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency measures cycles or oscillations per second and is expressed in hertz.

questions.question: Solve 3x = 27. What is x?
questions.explanation: Divide both sides of the equation by 3 to obtain x = 9.

questions.question: What is the square of 13?
questions.explanation: Thirteen multiplied by thirteen equals 169.

questions.question: What is the square root of 225?
questions.explanation: The positive square root is 15 because 15 × 15 = 225.

questions.question: Which expression is equivalent to (a + b)²?
questions.explanation: Expanding the product (a + b)(a + b) yields a² + 2ab + b².

questions.question: What is 2³ × 2²?
questions.explanation: With equal bases, add exponents: 2 to the fifth power equals 32.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cuboid 4 cm × 3 cm × 5 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume equals length × width × height = 60 cubic centimetres.

questions.question: A price rises from ₹80 to ₹100. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is ₹20, which is 20/80 = 25% of the original price.

questions.question: If two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°, what is the third?
questions.explanation: Interior angles of a triangle total 180 degrees, so the missing angle is 70.

questions.question: What is the reciprocal of 5/8?
questions.explanation: The reciprocal of a nonzero fraction exchanges numerator and denominator.

questions.question: What is the probability of obtaining a 3 on a fair six-sided die?
questions.explanation: One of six equally likely outcomes is a 3.

questions.question: Which of these is a human-made resource?
questions.explanation: A bridge is constructed by people using natural and other resources.

questions.question: Which category includes coal and petroleum?
questions.explanation: Coal and petroleum form over millions of years and are depleted by extraction.

questions.question: Which institution primarily makes national laws in India?
questions.explanation: Parliament legislates at the Union level subject to constitutional arrangements.

questions.question: What is the main role of an independent judiciary?
options: Interpret and apply law without improper interference
questions.explanation: Judicial independence supports impartial adjudication under law.

questions.question: Which year is commonly associated with the Battle of Plassey?
questions.explanation: The Battle of Plassey took place in 1757 and altered the East India Company's political position in Bengal.

questions.question: Why do historians distinguish primary and secondary sources?
options: Primary sources must always be accurate
They were created under different relationships to the events described
questions.explanation: The origin and purpose of a source matter when judging historical claims.

questions.question: What is the key purpose of a written constitution?
options: Specify fundamental structures, powers and limits of government
questions.explanation: Written constitutions establish basic rules and constrain public authority.

questions.question: Which agricultural practice helps protect soil on steep slopes?
questions.explanation: Terraces slow runoff and help retain soil and water on slopes.

questions.question: Which term refers to the right to vote in elections?
questions.explanation: Suffrage is the legal right to vote in an election.

questions.question: What is the meaning of sustainable development?
options: Meeting present needs while protecting future generations' ability to meet theirs
questions.explanation: Sustainable development balances present needs with future social and environmental well-being.

questions.question: Which state of matter has a fixed volume but takes the shape of its container?
questions.explanation: Liquids retain nearly constant volume but flow to take the container's shape.

questions.question: Which subatomic particle carries a negative electric charge?
questions.explanation: An electron has negative elementary electric charge.

questions.question: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
questions.explanation: Na comes from the Latin name natrium and denotes sodium.

questions.question: Which organelle is the principal site of ATP production during aerobic respiration in many eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate much of the ATP in aerobic cellular respiration.

questions.question: Which cell structure controls the movement of many substances into and out of the cell?
questions.explanation: The selectively permeable plasma membrane regulates exchange with the surroundings.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.explanation: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity and has units m/s².

questions.question: Which law relates force, mass and acceleration for constant mass?
questions.explanation: Newton's second law gives F = ma in the usual constant-mass case.

questions.question: Which tissue carries water and minerals upward in vascular plants?
questions.explanation: Xylem conducts water and dissolved mineral ions from roots through the plant.

questions.question: A solution is best described as which type of mixture?
questions.explanation: In a solution, solute and solvent form a macroscopically uniform mixture.

questions.question: Which organelle contains the main genetic material in most eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Most eukaryotic DNA is organised into chromosomes inside the nucleus.

questions.question: What is the degree of the polynomial 4x³ − 2x + 7?
questions.explanation: The highest power of x with a nonzero coefficient is 3.

questions.question: Which is a zero of the polynomial x − 5?
questions.explanation: Substituting x = 5 makes x − 5 equal to zero.

questions.question: What is the value of (−3)²?
questions.explanation: Squaring a negative number multiplies two negatives, giving a positive result.

questions.question: Which coordinates represent the origin in the Cartesian plane?
questions.explanation: The x-axis and y-axis intersect at the point (0,0).

questions.question: What is the sum of the interior angles of a triangle?
questions.explanation: Every Euclidean triangle has an angle sum of 180 degrees.

questions.question: What is the distance along the x-axis between (2,0) and (8,0)?
questions.explanation: The distance is the absolute difference of x-coordinates, 8 − 2 = 6.

questions.question: What is the median of 2, 6, 9, 11 and 15?
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value in the ordered list of five numbers.

questions.question: What is the mode of 3, 4, 4, 7 and 9?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value occurring most frequently.

questions.question: What is the volume of a cube with edge length 3 cm?
questions.explanation: Volume of a cube is edge cubed, so 3³ = 27 cm³.

questions.question: If x = 2 and y = −1, what is 3x + 2y?
questions.explanation: Substituting gives 3 × 2 + 2 × (−1) = 4.

questions.question: Which document is the supreme law of India?
questions.explanation: The Constitution establishes the foundation and limits of public authority.

questions.question: What does universal adult franchise mean?
options: All eligible adults can vote without discrimination on specified grounds
questions.explanation: Universal adult franchise extends voting rights to eligible adults subject to lawful conditions such as age and citizenship.

questions.question: What is the major cause of Earth's seasons?
options: Axial tilt combined with revolution around the Sun
questions.explanation: The tilt of Earth's axis changes the angle and duration of sunlight through the year.

questions.question: Which region commonly receives high rainfall from moist monsoon winds striking a mountain barrier?
questions.explanation: Orographic uplift cools moist air, encouraging condensation and rainfall on windward slopes.

questions.question: What is gross domestic product in broad terms?
options: Value of final goods and services produced within a country over a period
questions.explanation: GDP measures final production within domestic boundaries during a specified interval.

questions.question: What is a constitutional right?
options: A promise made only by an advertiser
A protection recognised in a constitution
questions.explanation: Constitutional rights derive legal force from constitutional provisions.

questions.question: Which economic activity belongs to the tertiary sector?
questions.explanation: Transport provides a service and is part of the tertiary sector.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an election commission?
options: Administer elections under the legal framework
questions.explanation: An election commission is responsible for administering elections according to applicable law.

questions.question: Which is a factor of production?
questions.explanation: Labour is human effort used in producing goods and services.

questions.question: What is a democracy?
options: A system where only one family can ever govern
A system where political authority is accountable through public participation and institutions
questions.explanation: Democratic governance involves popular participation, accountable institutions and political equality.

sets.subject: Science
sets.topic: Chemical reactions, electricity and life processes

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of water?
questions.explanation: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.question: Which process usually involves gain of oxygen by a substance?
questions.explanation: Oxidation traditionally includes the addition of oxygen and more generally electron loss.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
questions.explanation: Electrical resistance is measured in ohms.

questions.question: According to Ohm's law at constant conditions, voltage equals what?
questions.explanation: Ohm's law is V = IR for an ohmic conductor at constant physical conditions.

questions.question: Which organ is the main site of gas exchange in the human respiratory system?
questions.explanation: Oxygen and carbon dioxide diffuse across alveoli in the lungs.

questions.question: Which molecule carries hereditary information in most organisms?
questions.explanation: DNA stores genetic instructions in almost all cellular organisms.

questions.question: What is the principal role of chlorophyll in photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll pigments absorb light that powers photosynthetic reactions.

questions.question: Which lens is commonly used to correct myopia?
questions.explanation: A diverging concave lens can shift the image onto the retina for myopic vision.

questions.question: Which is an example of an acid-base neutralisation product?
questions.explanation: Many reactions between an acid and a base produce salt and water.

questions.question: In a food chain, which organisms are primary producers?
options: Green plants and other photosynthetic organisms
questions.explanation: Photosynthetic producers convert sunlight into chemical energy that supports food webs.

questions.question: What is the value of x if x² − 9 = 0 and x is positive?
questions.explanation: The solutions are ±3, and the positive one is 3.

questions.question: What is sin 30°?
questions.explanation: The sine of 30 degrees in a right triangle is one half.

questions.question: What is cos 60°?
questions.explanation: In a 30–60–90 triangle, the cosine of the 60-degree angle is the adjacent-to-hypotenuse ratio, 1/2.

questions.question: What is the discriminant of ax² + bx + c = 0?
questions.explanation: The discriminant D = b² − 4ac determines the nature of quadratic roots.

questions.question: What is the distance between (0,0) and (3,4)?
questions.explanation: The Pythagorean distance is √(3² + 4²) = 5.

questions.question: What is the sum of the first 10 positive integers?
questions.explanation: The arithmetic-series formula n(n + 1)/2 gives 10 × 11/2 = 55.

questions.question: A circle has radius 7 cm. What is its circumference?
questions.explanation: Circumference is 2πr, giving 14π cm when r = 7 cm.

questions.question: What is the probability of drawing an ace from a standard 52-card deck?
questions.explanation: There are four aces among 52 cards, so probability = 4/52 = 1/13.

questions.question: Which value is the arithmetic mean of 2, 4, 6, 8?
questions.explanation: Adding 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 gives 20; dividing by four observations gives 5.

questions.question: If two triangles have corresponding sides in the same ratio, what condition is satisfied?
options: Every angle is a right angle
questions.explanation: Proportional corresponding sides establish SSS similarity of triangles.

questions.question: In which year did India become independent from British colonial rule?
questions.explanation: India attained independence on 15 August 1947.

questions.question: What is federalism?
options: Division of governmental powers between different levels
Rule solely by a single municipal council
questions.explanation: Federalism distributes authority between Union and regional governments under a constitution.

questions.question: What is sustainable development?
options: Complete use of every fossil fuel today
Development meeting present needs without undermining future generations
questions.explanation: Sustainability balances present development with long-term social and environmental needs.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Reserve Bank of India?
questions.explanation: The RBI is India's central bank and helps implement monetary policy.

questions.question: What are tertiary-sector activities?
options: Services such as transport and banking
questions.explanation: The tertiary sector provides services rather than directly extracting or manufacturing goods.

questions.question: Which measure compares a country's average output per person?
questions.explanation: Per capita GDP is GDP divided by population and is only one indicator of development.

questions.question: Which is an example of power sharing in a democracy?
options: Authority shared between Union and state governments
Only one person making all decisions
questions.explanation: Constitutional division of powers is an important form of power sharing.

questions.question: Which body is directly elected to represent constituencies in the Lok Sabha?
questions.explanation: Lok Sabha members are elected from parliamentary constituencies.

questions.question: What do historians call the early-twentieth-century Indian movement led by Gandhi after the Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh concerns?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement began in 1920 in the broader national struggle.

questions.question: What is globalisation in an economic context?
options: Increasing interconnection of economies through trade, investment and production
questions.explanation: Economic globalisation links production, finance and trade across national boundaries.

questions.question: What is the slope of a position–time graph?
questions.explanation: The slope gives change in position divided by change in time, which is velocity.

questions.question: For a body starting from rest at constant acceleration a, what is its velocity after time t?
questions.explanation: The kinematic relation is v = u + at; with u = 0 it becomes v = at.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of work?
questions.explanation: Work is measured in joules, equivalent to newton metres.

questions.question: What does Newton's third law state?
options: Interaction forces occur in equal and opposite pairs on different bodies
Mass is the same as weight
The net force is always zero
questions.explanation: For every force one body exerts on another, there is an equal and opposite force on the first body.

questions.question: What is the kinetic energy of a mass m moving at speed v?
questions.explanation: Classical translational kinetic energy is one half times mass times speed squared.

questions.question: What is the acceleration of free fall near Earth's surface approximately?
questions.explanation: The magnitude of gravitational acceleration close to Earth's surface is about 9.8 metres per second squared.

questions.question: A body travels in a circle at constant speed. Why does it accelerate?
questions.explanation: Acceleration results from a change in velocity, including a change in direction.

questions.question: What physical quantity is conserved in an isolated collision system?
questions.explanation: In the absence of external net force, total momentum is conserved even if kinetic energy changes.

questions.question: What is the dimension of speed?
questions.explanation: Speed is distance travelled per unit time and has dimension L T⁻¹.

questions.question: When is mechanical work done by a constant force zero?
options: When displacement is perpendicular to the force
questions.explanation: Work W = Fs cos θ, so it is zero at a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: What is Avogadro's constant approximately?
questions.explanation: One mole contains approximately 6.022 × 10²³ specified entities.

questions.question: What determines the atomic number of an element?
options: Number of protons in its nucleus
questions.explanation: The proton count identifies the chemical element.

questions.question: Which particle is neutral?
questions.explanation: A neutron is electrically neutral, unlike the positively charged proton and negatively charged electron.

questions.question: What is an isotope?
options: Atoms of the same element with different neutron numbers
Atoms with completely different proton numbers
questions.explanation: Isotopes share atomic number but differ in neutron count and mass number.

questions.question: Which bond involves substantial transfer of electrons between atoms?
questions.explanation: An ionic bond is associated with electron transfer and electrostatic attraction of ions.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula of sodium chloride?
questions.explanation: Sodium chloride consists of sodium and chloride ions in a 1:1 ratio.

questions.question: Which quantity is the molar mass of carbon-12 atoms in grams per mole?
questions.explanation: Carbon-12 has a molar mass of exactly 12 grams per mole in customary textbook rounding.

questions.question: What is the usual maximum number of electrons in an s subshell?
questions.explanation: An s subshell contains one orbital, holding at most two electrons.

questions.question: Which change is exothermic?
options: A reaction that always absorbs heat
A reaction that releases heat to surroundings
questions.explanation: Exothermic processes transfer heat from the system to its surroundings.

questions.question: What is the pH of pure water near 25°C approximately?
questions.explanation: Pure water at about 25 degrees Celsius is neutral and has pH close to 7.

questions.question: What is the fundamental structural and functional unit of living organisms?
questions.explanation: Cells are the basic functional units of cellular life.

questions.question: Which organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes translate messenger RNA into proteins.

questions.question: Which pigment is central to oxygenic photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a participates in the photosynthetic reaction centres.

questions.question: Which molecule carries most of the usable energy released during cellular respiration?
questions.explanation: ATP couples energy-releasing reactions to cellular work.

questions.question: What is the function of xylem in plants?
questions.explanation: Xylem tissue conducts water and minerals, especially from roots upward.

questions.question: What do enzymes generally do in living systems?
options: Lower activation energy of biochemical reactions
Change the equilibrium constant at fixed temperature
questions.explanation: Enzymes accelerate reactions by lowering activation energy without changing the equilibrium position.

questions.question: Which structure controls opening and closing of a stoma?
questions.explanation: Guard cells regulate the stomatal aperture and influence gas exchange and water loss.

questions.question: Which human blood component is chiefly responsible for oxygen transport?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin inside red blood cells carries most oxygen in blood.

questions.question: What is osmosis?
options: Net water movement across a selectively permeable membrane down water-potential gradient
questions.explanation: Osmosis is water movement through a selectively permeable membrane from higher to lower water potential.

questions.question: Which taxonomic rank is more specific than genus?
questions.explanation: In the usual hierarchy, species is ranked below genus and is more specific.

questions.question: What is opportunity cost?
options: Price of every available option added together
Value of the next best alternative forgone
questions.explanation: Choosing one option sacrifices the benefit obtainable from the next best alternative.

questions.question: What does the law of demand generally state, other things equal?
options: Quantity demanded tends to fall as price rises
Quantity demanded always rises with price
questions.explanation: A typical downward-sloping demand relationship means consumers demand less at higher prices, other factors unchanged.

questions.question: What is a budget constraint?
options: A list of all government laws
Combinations of goods affordable with given income and prices
The maximum population of a country
questions.explanation: A consumer's budget constraint limits affordable combinations based on income and prices.

questions.question: Which is an example of a fixed cost in the short run?
questions.explanation: A fixed cost does not vary with the quantity produced over the relevant short-run range.

questions.question: What does GDP measure?
options: Number of banks in a country
Value of final goods and services produced within an economy during a period
questions.explanation: GDP avoids double-counting intermediate goods and records final domestic production.

questions.question: What is inflation?
options: Sustained rise in the general price level
Any fall in a commodity price
questions.explanation: Inflation refers to an increase in an overall price index over time.

questions.question: What does the primary sector mainly include?
questions.explanation: The primary sector directly draws on natural resources.

questions.question: What is a statistical sample?
options: Subset of observations selected from a population
questions.explanation: A sample is a subset used to learn about a larger population.

questions.question: Which average is the middle ordered observation?
questions.explanation: The median splits ordered observations into lower and upper halves.

questions.question: What is the meaning of human capital?
options: Skills, health and knowledge embodied in people
questions.explanation: Education, skills and health are major components of human capital.

questions.question: What is archaeology primarily concerned with?
options: Material evidence of past human societies
questions.explanation: Archaeologists study artefacts, features and remains to understand past societies.

questions.question: Which change is associated with early farming settlements?
questions.explanation: Agriculture and domestication supported more settled ways of life in many regions.

questions.question: What is the principal purpose of dating an archaeological layer?
options: Establish its place in a sequence of events
questions.explanation: Relative and absolute dating help establish chronology for archaeological contexts.

questions.question: Why are inscriptions valuable historical evidence?
options: They provide contemporary or near-contemporary written records
They eliminate need for other sources
They record all events of a period
questions.explanation: Inscriptions can illuminate rulers, donors, institutions and languages, though they must be read critically.

questions.question: Which river valley is associated with ancient Egyptian civilisation?
questions.explanation: Ancient Egyptian settlements and state development were strongly tied to the Nile valley.

questions.question: What does a historical primary source mean?
options: Evidence created during or close to the period being examined
questions.explanation: Primary sources provide direct evidence but still require contextual interpretation.

questions.question: What is the significance of a stratigraphic layer in archaeology?
options: It helps establish relative order of deposits
It gives every object's exact age automatically
questions.explanation: Layer relationships often reveal relative sequence; later disturbance can complicate interpretation.

questions.question: What is a city-state in historical study?
options: An autonomous political unit centred on a city and its territory
questions.explanation: City-states organised political authority around urban centres and nearby territories.

questions.question: Which material was a major early writing surface in Mesopotamia?
questions.explanation: Cuneiform inscriptions were commonly impressed on clay tablets in ancient Mesopotamia.

questions.question: Why should historians compare multiple sources?
options: Different sources may reflect different purposes, perspectives and limits
questions.explanation: Cross-checking helps evaluate biases, contexts and points of agreement.

questions.question: What is Coulomb's law about?
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law relates electrostatic force to the product of charges and inverse square of separation.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electric potential difference?
questions.explanation: A volt is one joule of energy transferred per coulomb of charge.

questions.question: What is the equivalent resistance of two 2 Ω resistors in series?
questions.explanation: Resistances connected in series add, giving 2 + 2 = 4 ohms.

questions.question: What is the equivalent resistance of two 4 Ω resistors in parallel?
questions.explanation: For equal resistors in parallel the equivalent resistance is half an individual resistance.

questions.question: What is the direction of the magnetic field around a long straight current-carrying wire?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field forms concentric circles according to the right-hand thumb rule.

questions.question: What is electromagnetic induction?
options: Conversion of light to sound only
Production of emf by changing magnetic flux through a circuit
Transfer of heat without temperature difference
questions.explanation: Faraday's law connects induced electromotive force with rate of change of magnetic flux.

questions.question: What is the speed of light in vacuum approximately?
questions.explanation: Light travels in vacuum at about three hundred million metres per second.

questions.question: Which type of lens can bring parallel rays to a focus in air?
questions.explanation: A converging convex lens brings parallel incident rays to its focal region.

questions.question: What is the refractive index of a medium defined as?
options: Speed of sound divided by speed of light
Speed of light in vacuum divided by its phase speed in the medium
questions.explanation: The refractive index n = c/v for light's phase velocity in a medium.

questions.question: Which phenomenon demonstrates the wave nature of light?
questions.explanation: Interference patterns result from superposition of coherent light waves.

questions.question: What is molarity?
options: Moles of solute per litre of solution
Moles of gas per kilogram of air only
questions.explanation: Molarity is amount of dissolved solute divided by total solution volume in litres.

questions.question: What is a catalyst's usual effect on reaction rate?
options: It provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
questions.explanation: A catalyst can speed forward and reverse reactions without changing the equilibrium constant.

questions.question: What is the SI unit of electrical conductance?
questions.explanation: Electrical conductance is reciprocal resistance and is measured in siemens.

questions.question: Which process occurs at the anode of an electrochemical cell?
questions.explanation: Oxidation always occurs at the anode, whether the cell is galvanic or electrolytic.

questions.question: Which process occurs at the cathode?
questions.explanation: Reduction occurs at the cathode in electrochemical systems.

questions.question: What does an increase in temperature often do to a reaction rate?
options: Increase it by raising the proportion of energetic collisions
questions.explanation: Higher temperature commonly increases reaction rates by altering collision energy distributions.

questions.question: What is the molecular formula of ethanol?
questions.explanation: Ethanol contains two carbons, six hydrogens and one oxygen atom.

questions.question: Which compound is an aldehyde?
questions.explanation: Ethanal contains the terminal −CHO functional group.

questions.question: What is the oxidation number of oxygen in most ordinary oxides?
questions.explanation: Oxygen commonly has oxidation state −2, with exceptions such as peroxides.

questions.question: Which interaction is chiefly responsible for the high boiling point of water relative to comparable hydrides?
questions.explanation: Strong intermolecular hydrogen bonding raises the energy needed to separate water molecules.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of heredity?
questions.explanation: Genes are inherited DNA sequences that affect traits through their products or regulatory roles.

questions.question: What is a genotype?
options: Genetic makeup at one or more loci
Number of cells in a body
questions.explanation: Genotype refers to the genetic information possessed for specified loci.

questions.question: Which base is found in RNA instead of thymine?
questions.explanation: RNA typically contains uracil where DNA contains thymine.

questions.question: What is transcription?
options: Synthesis of RNA using DNA as a template
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase reads a DNA template to produce an RNA molecule.

questions.question: What is translation in molecular biology?
options: Creation of an organism from soil
Synthesis of a polypeptide using an mRNA template
questions.explanation: Ribosomes use mRNA codons to assemble amino acids into a polypeptide.

questions.question: Which process generally increases genetic variation in sexual reproduction?
questions.explanation: Independent assortment and crossing over in meiosis create new combinations of alleles.

questions.question: What is a food web?
questions.explanation: Food webs represent multiple interconnected pathways of energy transfer in an ecosystem.

questions.question: What is biomagnification?
options: Increase of body size in every species
Increasing concentration of some persistent pollutants at higher trophic levels
questions.explanation: Some persistent substances accumulate through feeding relationships and reach higher concentrations in predators.

questions.question: Which method introduces a chosen DNA sequence into a host using a vector?
questions.explanation: Recombinant DNA methods can place selected DNA into suitable vectors for propagation or expression.

questions.question: Which organ is a major site of immune cell development and maturation of T cells?
questions.explanation: The thymus is important for T-lymphocyte maturation, especially earlier in life.

questions.question: Which aggregate measures final production within domestic borders?
questions.explanation: GDP totals domestic value added in final goods and services for a period.

questions.question: What is monetary policy primarily concerned with?
options: Central bank management of money, credit and interest-rate conditions
questions.explanation: Monetary policy seeks macroeconomic goals by influencing financial and monetary conditions.

questions.question: Which institution issues most currency notes in India under the legal framework?
questions.explanation: The RBI issues banknotes except the one-rupee note, issued by the Government of India.

questions.question: What is a fiscal deficit broadly?
options: Government's total expenditure less total receipts excluding borrowing
questions.explanation: Fiscal deficit indicates the government's borrowing requirement under the budget definition.

questions.question: What does a balance of payments record?
options: Economic transactions between residents and the rest of the world
questions.explanation: The balance of payments records current, capital and financial external transactions.

questions.question: What does depreciation mean for a floating exchange rate?
options: A fall in the value of a currency relative to others
questions.explanation: Currency depreciation makes it worth less compared with another currency under market movement.

questions.question: Which is a common development indicator alongside income?
questions.explanation: Health and education indicators complement income measures when comparing development.

questions.question: What is the marginal propensity to consume?
options: Total consumption divided by all wealth
Change in consumption divided by change in income
questions.explanation: MPC measures how much of an additional unit of income is spent on consumption.

questions.question: What is inflation targeting?
options: Setting identical prices for all goods
Monetary policy framework focused on a specified inflation objective
questions.explanation: An inflation-targeting framework uses policy instruments to steer inflation toward a stated target.

questions.question: Which is an example of public infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Transport infrastructure supports broader economic and social activities.

questions.question: When was the Indian National Congress established?
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885, with the first session at Bombay.

questions.question: Who led the Salt March of 1930?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's Dandi March challenged the colonial salt law during the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.question: What is the main aim of historical source criticism?
options: Assume all official records are unbiased
Evaluate origin, context, reliability and bias of evidence
questions.explanation: Source criticism considers who produced a record, why, when and for whom.

questions.question: Which 1942 movement called for an end to British rule in India?
questions.explanation: The Quit India resolution was adopted in August 1942 in the context of World War II.

questions.question: What does the term Constituent Assembly refer to in modern Indian history?
options: Committee that ran the East India Company in 1757
Body that debated and drafted India's Constitution
A group that created the Mughal empire
questions.explanation: The Constituent Assembly deliberated and adopted the Constitution of India.

questions.question: When did India's Constitution come into effect?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was adopted in November 1949 but commenced on 26 January 1950.

questions.question: Which practice best supports reliable oral-history research?
options: Use only one phrase without context
Compare recollections with context and other evidence
questions.explanation: Oral accounts provide valuable perspectives but can be shaped by memory and circumstances.

questions.question: What historical event took place at Jallianwala Bagh in 1919?
options: British troops fired on a gathering in Amritsar
The First Battle of Panipat occurred
questions.explanation: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre occurred in Amritsar on 13 April 1919.

questions.question: What is the significance of an archive?
options: It is solely an amusement park
It preserves records useful for historical research
It guarantees every record is true
questions.explanation: Archives conserve documents and other materials whose provenance researchers must assess.

questions.question: Which statement about historical narratives is most accurate?
options: A popular story needs no evidence
They should be supported by evidence and remain open to revision
Only one type of document ever matters
questions.explanation: Historians evaluate multiple kinds of evidence and revise interpretations when warranted.
